newsitem.title: Australia: Australian debt rampant, scents further easing.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt rampant, scents further easing.

text.p: *Australian debt yields fell sharply across the curve after a weak set of retail trade data for April added fuel to talk that the Reserve Bank's easing cycle is not over yet.
*Australian dollar gets same vibes and tumbles.
Australian debt yields fell sharply across the curve after a weak set of retail trade data for April added fuel to talk that the Reserve Bank's easing cycle is not over yet.

Debt futures raced ahead after news that retail trade fell 1.7 percent, its first successive monthly fall in nearly four years, adding to the view that the firm patch seen in the economy at the start of the year has aleady crumbled.
"At best, the economy is flat," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank Australia.

September bill futures touched a high of 94.66, equating to a cash rate of 5.34 percent compared with official interest of 5.5 percent, while the December contract all but wiped out thoughts of a tightening by the end of the year.
The June three-year bond futures contract struck its highest level since February 1994 at 93.83 continuing the rally since last Friday's surprise official interest rate cut.
Long-dated yields also fell over 10 basis points and closed the differential to the U.S. to its lowest level in some three year at around the low 70 basis points.

Rory Robertson, interest rate strategist at Bankers Trust Australia, sees the market increasingly pricing in a further official rate cut with bank bills falling to 5.25 percent and three-yields falling to below 6.0 percent.

"The 10-year part of the curve is more difficult because of the influence of the U.S. market, but we are increasingly positive," he said. He expects yields here to fall back to 7.0 percent in the next couple of quarters and the spread to the U.S. down to 25 basis points.
His assumptions are based on Australian inflation being 1.0 percent below that of the U.S. by year-end.

The strong performance of the local market saw it leave the rest of the dollar bloc for dust, and it outperformed Thursday's rally in Canadian debt on a firm Canadian dollar. This market has been under a cloud on the threat of a tightening by the Fed and ahead of next week's general election.
